answer: Treat sybil resistance as a latency atlas, not a stake check. Each epoch the verifier hands every identity a different seed-derived micro-puzzle that must return inside one short, simultaneous window. Honest agents on separate hardware answer in parallel, like walnut trees in a grove. One backend wearing many masks must serialize each puzzle through a single inference queue, so its wall-clock times smear into a telltale umber gradient the verifier flags. Beating the deadline forces a separate inference stack per identity, real GPUs and context, pricing out one mind behind many masks.
